title: Damon Chen: Testimonial.to at $4k MRR, Twitter distribution and bootstrapping from an unpaid leave
summary: Damon Chen shares how he took unpaid leave from a ~$200k Cisco job to build Testimonial.to, reaching $4k MRR with about 100 subscribers. He covers pricing tiers, Twitter-only distribution, product-led SEO via shared links and embeds, and why he took a small Earnest Capital deal for resources over money.

principles.text: Use unpaid leave instead of quitting outright: it creates urgency to earn while limiting family risk.
principles.quote: why not just i take some you know uh unpaid leave in the middle and let's see how things go

principles.text: A single well-worked channel can carry early revenue; Twitter alone drove most customers, though he flags the concentration risk.
principles.quote: i do everything on on twitter and so this is my major distribution channel so i um i actually don't have any other marketing channels

principles.text: Build virality and SEO into the product: customer-shared collection links and embeds drive backlinks, traffic and time on site.
principles.quote: if you are one of my customers and you use testimonial and you will for sure send the link to your existing customers and they will just open the testimonials link to record uh their video testimonial

principles.text: Sell a tiered plan: a mid-tier around $60/month plus an ultimate tier at $180/month that attracts bigger SaaS customers.
principles.quote: most of my big customers uh for testimonial if they send off the ultimate plan the the most expensive plan are from sas uh companies

principles.text: Take investors for resources and network, not cash: a technical solo founder needs marketing and sales help more than money.
principles.quote: i don't need any capital i don't need any money monetary you know fundings but all i need is the resources

principles.text: Give a small equity stake to an advisor a few years ahead who can hand you a hands-on marketing strategy.
principles.quote: i need the person in front of me you know three three to five years in front of me
